title: Classical-Quantum Average-Case Complexity Relation
summary: Known total-function query-complexity relations do not settle whether classical and quantum average-case complexities are polynomially related in general for this cryptanalytic setting.

formal_statement.body: For ideal-model symmetric cryptanalytic problems in the relevant average-case setting, determine whether a polynomial relationship exists in general between the classical and quantum average-case complexities. Known randomized-versus-quantum query-complexity relations for total functions do not directly settle this average-case cryptanalytic setting.

scope.domain: Mathematical foundations of classical and quantum average-case complexity in ideal-model symmetric cryptanalysis.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether a polynomial relationship exists in general between the classical and quantum average-case complexities in the relevant cryptanalytic setting.

citations.label: Beyond quadratic speedups in quantum attacks on symmetric schemes

progress.summary: The source contrasts its average-case cryptanalytic setting with known randomized-versus-quantum query-complexity relations for total functions and states that no general polynomial relation is currently known.
citation_labels: Xavier Bonnetain et al., Beyond quadratic speedups in quantum attacks on symmetric schemes
